question.text: Emergency double-balloon enteroscopy combined with real-time viewing of capsule endoscopy: a feasible combined approach in acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding?
question.context: There are few data concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) and its usefulness in the management of severe acute obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB). The aim of this retrospective study was to evaluate emergency DBE and capsule endoscopy (CE) in patients with overt OGIB, analyzing the feasibility of this combined approach. Emergency DBE in patients with overt OGIB was defined as performance within 24 h of symptom onset. We reported 27 patients (16 men, mean age: 64.6 ± 17.9 years) with overt severe bleeding who underwent 29 emergency DBE (22 anterograde, 7 retrograde). Of 27 patients, 16 (59.3%) underwent CE with real time (RT) viewing. Patients were diagnosed with the following: Dieulafoy's lesion (DL; n = 11, 40.7%), angioectasia (n = 7, 25.9%), tumors (n = 4, 14.8%), diverticulum (n = 3, 11.1%), ulcers (n = 2, 7.4%). We diagnosed 23 lesions amenable to endoscopic hemostasis and successfully treated 21 of them (77.8%). DL detection rate was statistically higher in the emergency DBE group than in OGIB patients with DBE done 24 h after symptom onset (40.7% vs 0.9%, respectively, P < 0.001). Combined approach with RT viewing by CE correctly modified DBE management in four patients (25%).

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The clinical case describes a study evaluating the feasibility of combining emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) with real-time viewing of capsule endoscopy (CE) in patients with acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB). The study found that emergency DBE was feasible and that the combined approach with RT viewing by CE correctly modified DBE management in four patients. This suggests that the combined approach is useful.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: Combined approach with RT viewing by CE correctly modified DBE management in four patients (25%).
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While the study mentions various potential causes of OGIB (Dieulafoy's lesion, angioectasia, tumors, diverticulum, ulcers), the primary focus is on the feasibility and utility of the combined approach. The study's findings support the use of the combined approach, making other diagnoses less relevant in the context of the question.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that emergency double-balloon enteroscopy combined with real-time capsule endoscopy is feasible and effective in managing acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding. The high detection rate of Dieulafoy's lesions within 24 hours and successful hemostasis in 77.8% of cases supports its clinical utility.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: The 40.7% detection rate of Dieulafoy's lesions in the emergency DBE group compared to 0.9% in delayed DBE (P < 0.001) shows the time-sensitive nature of this approach.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that emergency DBE within 24 hours of symptom onset is feasible and effective in diagnosing and treating severe overt OGIB, with a high detection rate of Dieulafoy's lesions and successful hemostasis in 77.8% of treatable lesions. The combined approach with real-time capsule endoscopy further improved diagnostic accuracy in 25% of cases, supporting its feasibility and clinical utility.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: The combined approach with real-time capsule endoscopy correctly modified DBE management in four patients (25%), indicating added value and feasibility.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Dieulafoy's lesion, angioectasia, tumors, diverticulum, and ulcers were considered; Dieulafoy's was most prevalent (40.7%) and significantly more common in emergency DBE vs delayed DBE, supporting the approach's efficacy.

openbio_8b.clinical_reasoning: The combined approach of emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) and capsule endoscopy (CE) with real-time viewing is feasible and effective in the management of severe acute obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB). This approach allows for rapid diagnosis and endoscopic hemostasis of the bleeding lesion, which can be life-saving in critically ill patients. The higher detection rate of Dieulafoy's lesion in the emergency DBE group compared to those undergoing DBE 24 hours after symptom onset highlights the utility of this combined approach in identifying the source of bleeding in a timely manner.
openbio_8b.critical_evidence: The detection rate of Dieulafoy's lesion was significantly higher in the emergency DBE group than in OGIB patients who underwent DBE 24 hours after symptom onset.
openbio_8b.differential_considered: None of the options provided are correct. The correct answer is A based on the evidence provided in the clinical case.

olmo3_7b.differential_considered: Dieulafoy's lesion (the most common cause of acute obscure bleeding), angioectasia, tumors, and diverticulitis were considered, but the lack of a 100% success rate for the combined approach and the rarity of DL detection without prior CE makes a definitive "yes" or "definitive best option" unsupported.
